propositions: The ownership and field-consumption gates currently run in disparate places: check_config_ownership.py runs nowhere, and check_config_reads.py runs only in a standalone CI workflow step with an ee2a skip guard, risking double-run and CI-provider lock-in.

Both gates must be invoked from the portable local make lint target so they execute in a single place and CI runs them through the existing make lint step, eliminating the standalone workflow step and the double-run risk.

The ee2a if-present guard protecting pre-slice-C1 Gerrit patchsets becomes obsolete because a patchset's own Makefile will lack the gate invocations if it predates this change, so make lint naturally skips them without a missing-file failure.

The parity test anchored to the workflow step must be re-anchored to assert the Makefile lint target wires both gate invocations, and extended to verify removal of either gate or make lint from their respective locations fails the parity check.
